design.second_asset: the detector's own second-asset gap per venue: Bitfinex ETH vs Coinbase ETH, Coinbase ETH vs Bitstamp ETH, Binance.US USDT/USD vs Bitstamp USDT/USD
design.b2_note: B2 has no bps threshold; its curve is indexed by k
design.b3_note: B3 exists for Bitfinex only (USTUSD from 2018-11); pooled B3 is the Bitfinex point alone
design.pooled: sum of counts over the venues where the method exists

exposure.binance_us_note: Binance.US: detector and B1 both have 1 false-alarm episode(s); the rates 1.31 vs 1.26 differ only because the detector is evaluated on 6,683 hours (BTC and the second-asset gap both present) and B1 on 6,983 hours (BTC gap present).
exposure.recall_note: A positive is covered when at least half of its truth-window days have evaluated hours. Under D1 reference-side Bitstamp labels (BST-*) are positives at every venue measured against Bitstamp, so the pooled covered count adds each such label once per venue where it is covered. B2 loses its first 30 days of each series to the trailing window, which can change coverage.
exposure.false_alarm_denominator: evaluated venue-hours / HOURS_PER_YEAR; the module divisor is 24 x 365.25 = 8,766, and the _at_8760 columns repeat the rate with 8,760.

excluded.CB-2019-01: GBP rail; the monitored quantity is the USD ledger (amendment D1)

timeline.framing: The price measured the impairment continuously from 2018-10-10 (first day the daily Bitfinex-Bitstamp BTC gap exceeded 100 bps in 2018-H2), while the documented disclosure of the loss came on 2019-04-25 (NYAG complaint). The Noble Bank and deposit-pause reports (2018-09-30, 2018-10-11) were public earlier and are labels, not prices.
